newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, crop outlook improves.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, crop outlook improves.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed sharply down after dipping to its lowest level for more than two years, weakened partly by a bearish acreage report issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Spring wheat acreage was estimated by USDA at 19.2 million acres, above the upper end of the 17.6 to 18.8 million acre range in a Reuter survey of analysts.
"The acreage number was a surprise to a lot of people. There is also a feeling that spring wheat is making some bushels out there with the kind of rain we've had," one floor trader said.
July wheat fell to a low of $3.67-1/2 a bushel, the lowest level for the nearby contract since April 1995. It closed off 7-1/4 cents at $3.71-3/4.
Floor sources said mill buying helped to limit losses with ADM buying 2.0 million bushels September. Sellers included Benson Quinn (2.0 million September).
Volume was estimated at 30.36 million bushels, up from 26.47 million bushels on Friday.
